newsitem.title: USA: MSRB to meet Thursday with bond dealers on G-37.
newsitem.headline: MSRB to meet Thursday with bond dealers on G-37.

text.p: Officials of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board agreed to meet this week with a task force of muni bond dealers to discuss dealer concerns with the panel's "pay-to-play" rule G-37, MSRB and dealer representatives said on Tuesday.

A key issue at the meeting, set for February 20 at 1100 EST, will be the rule's "look-back" provision, which says G-37's two-year ban on business can apply even to contributions made before an employee joins a particular bond firm, MSRB and dealer representatives said.

Edmund Pendleton, director of media relations for PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, which requested the meeting, said 15 to 20 member's of PSA's G-37 Model Supervisory Procedures Task Force will attend the session with MSRB officials.
He said the meeting is a followup to a presentation by MSRB executive director Christopher Taylor at a PSA meeting for regional bond dealers in Orlando in the last two weeks.
Bond dealers have questions about how to enforce the look-back provision, Pendleton said, referring to one of the most controversial sections of MSRB's pay-to-play rule.
Enacted in April 1994, rule G-37 bars muni dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from engaging in negotiated business for two years with those governments.

The ban applies even if an employee gave a contribution to an issuer official before he or she came on board at a particular bond firm, as long as the contribution was within the last two years, MSRB said in a recent interpretation of rule G-37.
Bond firms "want greater clarification on how to enforce" that provision, Pendleton said.
"We look forward to sitting down with them and hearing what they have to say, how they feel (the rule) is operating," Taylor said.
PSA looks forward to a "constructive" meeting, Pendleton said.
